feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 5 (±0.036 m span, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 3.6, kd 0.9) scored 653.3, the best so far. Its oval was 20/20 at 1.85 s and its s-bend 18/20 with steering_oscillation 0.335. Its slalom was 0/20 with 1.0 line-loss events and max_error 0.0644. Iteration 3 showed that lead 0.04 m hurt the oval (14/20) and the s-bend (6/20), so shortening the lead is ruled out. The 0.07 m lead is a single test of a longer look-ahead. Next-race rules: if slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 or max_error drops below 0.06, keep the lead at 0.07 m and try to tune for finishes, reporting slalom completion_time. If slalom line loss is unchanged at about 1.0 with max_error at 0.06 or more, lead is not the limit, so return the lead to 0.06 m and test the yaw response. If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 with no slalom gain, return the lead to 0.06 m, since jitter cost outweighs the benefit.
requested_changes: Keep the lead at y = 0.07 m only if slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 or max_error drops below 0.06. If it does not, return to y = 0.06 m (iteration 5 values), since lead 0.04 m was worse on every track.

If the slalom is unchanged at about 1.0 line-loss events with max_error at or above 0.06 at lead 0.07 m, return to y = 0.06 m and test yaw inertia: mass 0.6 kg with body_length 0.12 m, keeping the iteration 5 span and drivetrain. Evidence: the slalom has failed at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 across five variants.

If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 at lead 0.07 m (iteration 5 measured 0.335 at 0.06 m), return the lead to 0.06 m. Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m, since the iteration 4 and 5 oval results (20/20 at about 1.82 to 1.85 s) show the drivetrain is safe at that track.
